newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices surge on compressor outage.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices surge on compressor outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for September surged in Wednesday trade in anticipation of a major scheduled outage on the NOVA intra-Alberta pipeline network, traders said.
The outage, of the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day Knight compressor station on NOVA's Edson mainline in northwestern Alberta, was slated to last 36 hours starting late Wednesday.

Gas for September delivery at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.26 per gigajoule range, up from C$0.93/0.94 last week. October gas was talked at C$1.165/C$1.18 per GJ, up from C$1.15/1.16.
Spot prices last week were hammered by maintenance at AECO, which severely restricted injections and withdrawals.

A Calgary-based trader said injections at all three Alberta facilties were at about 800 million cubic feet per day on Wednesday with AECO back up, which was also giving new strength to domestic prices.
At the borders, gas at Niagara was talked at about US$2.11 per million British thermal units, up 11 cents from last week.
One trader of eastern Candian gas said prices seemed to be mirroring the recent rise of the NYMEX October futures price.
"The screen is having a big influence on the cash price," he said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
